rca of the issue: User perception of a font-weight difference between the two Education subtitle lines is NOT reflected in the DOM/CSS. getComputedStyle on both '.edu-sub' elements returns identical fontWeight ('400'), fontStyle ('italic'), fontFamily, fontSize ('15.68px'), color ('rgb(74, 91, 107)'), and opacity ('1'). The second line contains an inline span.edu-arrow (1px horizontal rule, ~18.8px wide, display:inline-block) between 'Aviation Science (Pilot)' and 'Aviation Management'. This decorative element does NOT change font-weight (span inherits 400) but visually splits the italic text into two shorter segments with additional whitespace, which — combined with differing character composition and glyph density between the two sentences — creates the optical impression that line 2 is lighter/thinner. Mitigation options if desired: (a) remove span.edu-arrow, (b) replace the em-dash-like connector with a text character rendered in the same italic 400 weight, or (c) apply matching decoration symmetrically on line 1.
